# Volume 5 — CHAPTER XII. AN EXPLANATION AND A DARE

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

The Rev. Dr. Cooper delivered his sermon at Glen St. Agnes the following night, filling the Presbyterian Church with an immense gathering of folks from both close by and distant places. Renowned as a highly gifted orator, the Reverend Doctor presented an exceedingly erudite and powerful message, adhering to the age-old proverb which suggests a preacher ought to pack his finest garments for urban trips and his finest homilies for rural ones. Nevertheless, as the congregation returned to their houses that evening, Dr. Cooper’s sermon was not the subject of their conversation. Every bit of it had slipped their minds entirely.
{: #nw-v05-c12-p0000 }

Dr. Cooper finished his speech with an impassioned plea, cleared the sweat from his large forehead, uttered “Let us pray” in his renowned manner, and proceeded to offer the prayer. A brief moment of silence followed. The congregation of Glen St. Agnes church preserved the former custom of collecting the offering following the sermon rather than prior to it—primarily for the reason that this recent practice had been taken up by the Methodists first, and neither Miss Winifred nor Elder Clow would consent to imitate a path the Methodists had forged. Being responsible for passing the plates, Charles Baxter and Thomas Fairlie were just about to stand up. Having pulled out the sheet music for her anthem, the organist waited while the choir cleared its collective throat. All at once, Grace Ashdown stood up in the manse pew, stepped onto the pulpit platform, and turned toward the astonished crowd.
{: #nw-v05-c12-p0001 }

Miss Winifred started to stand up from her place before seating herself once more. Because her pew was positioned near the rear, she realized that whatever action or statement Grace intended to make would already be halfway accomplished or uttered prior to her arrival. Creating a scene any more embarrassing than necessary served no purpose. Directing a pained look toward Mrs. Dr. Carrow, followed by a second toward Deacon Warren belonging to the Methodist Church, Miss Winifred surrendered to the inevitability of yet another scandal.
{: #nw-v05-c12-p0002 }

“Provided that the youngster was merely clothed in a respectable manner,” her soul lamented.
{: #nw-v05-c12-p0003 }

Grace, after spilling ink on her fine frock, had calmly changed into a washed-out pink print garment from earlier days. A diagonal tear in her skirt had been mended using red embroidery thread, and the bottom edge had been unstitched, revealing a vivid band of original pink along the hemline. However, Grace was giving no thought to her attire whatsoever. A sudden wave of anxiety washed over her. An act that appeared simple in her mind proved quite difficult in truth. Facing that entire collection of fixed, inquiring glances, Grace almost lost her nerve. The illumination was so intense, the quietude so terrifying. It struck her that she might be unable to utter a sound after all. Yet she had to—it was imperative to free her father from doubt. Except—the speech refused to form.
{: #nw-v05-c12-p0004 }

From the manse pew, the small, pearl-pure face of Ida gleamed up at her in a beseeching manner. The Carrow children were completely astonished. Farther back beneath the gallery, Grace noticed the sweet graciousness present in the smile of Miss Clementine Ainslie, as well as the amusement displayed in that of Miss Harriet. Yet none of these things provided her with aid. It was Bertie Shakespeare Drew who rescued the circumstance. Bertie Shakespeare was seated in the gallery's front row, and he pulled a mockingly scornful face at Grace. Grace immediately pulled an appalling face right back at him, and because of her rage at being made faces at by Bertie Shakespeare, she lost her stage fright. Locating her voice, she spoke aloud both distinctly and courageously.
{: #nw-v05-c12-p0005 }

“I need to make something clear,” she stated, “and I wish to do it right away so everyone who listened to the previous story can hear this one. A rumor is going around that Ida and I remained at home this past Sunday to clean the house rather than attending Sunday School. It is true that we did—however, it was not our intention. The days of the week became confused in our minds. The blame lies entirely with Elder Baxter”—a reaction occurred in the pew belonging to Baxter—“since he proceeded to shift the prayer-meeting over to Wednesday evening, causing us to mistake Thursday for Friday and so forth, until Saturday seemed to us like Sunday. Rupert was bedridden with illness, as was Aunt Martha, meaning neither of them could set us straight. During all that rain on Saturday, we traveled to Sunday School, but not a soul arrived. After that, we decided we would perform our housecleaning on Monday to halt the gossip of old cats regarding the filthy state of the manse”—a broad reaction rippled throughout the whole church—“and that is what we accomplished. The reason I shook out the rugs inside the Methodist graveyard was that it offered a handy spot, not owing to any desire on my part to show disrespect toward the deceased. The departed aren't the ones who raised a commotion about this matter—the living ones are. Furthermore, it is unfair for a single one of you to fault my father regarding this, since he was out of town and unaware, and regardless, we believed the day to be Monday. He happens to be the finest father who ever existed anywhere, and our love for him fills our whole hearts.”
{: #nw-v05-c12-p0006 }

Grace’s confidence drained away as she broke into a sob. Hurrying down the stairs, she darted through the church’s side entrance. Outside, she found solace in the welcoming, star-filled summer evening, which eased the pain in her eyes and neck. A sense of great joy washed over her. The terrible clarification had been made at last, meaning all the people were aware that her father held no responsibility and that Ida and she had not been so sinful as to consciously perform housework on a Sunday.
{: #nw-v05-c12-p0007 }

Worshippers exchanged empty looks within the church, yet Thomas Fairlie stood and strode toward the altar with a rigid expression. He had a plain obligation; even if the heavens collapsed, the gathering of offerings had to proceed. It indeed took place; the anthem was performed by the choir, who felt a gloomy certainty that their song lacked any spark, while Dr. Cooper announced the final hymn and offered the blessing with much less enthusiasm than he typically displayed. A sense of comedy possessed the Reverend Doctor, who found himself amused by Grace’s actions. Furthermore, John Ashdown enjoyed widespread recognition among Presbyterian groups.
{: #nw-v05-c12-p0008 }

The following afternoon brought Mr. Ashdown back home, yet Grace managed to shock Glen St. Agnes once more prior to his arrival. Following the pressure and seriousness of Sunday evening, a rebound left her particularly brimming with what Miss Winifred would have termed “devilment” on Monday. Because of this, she challenged Edmund Carrow to travel down Main Street atop a pig, as she herself mounted a second one.
{: #nw-v05-c12-p0009 }

The pair of swine being referred to were two long, lean beasts, believed to be owned by the father of Bertie Shakespeare Drew, that had been lingering along the edge of the road near the parsonage for about fourteen days. Although Edmund had no desire to mount a pig through Glen St. Agnes, he was bound to execute any challenge Grace Ashdown set before him. Down the slope and through the settlement they rushed, Grace doubled over in hysterics atop her frightened mount, while Edmund turned bright red with humiliation. They bolted past the clergyman himself, who was just returning from the depot; because he was slightly more alert and less preoccupied than was typical—a result of chatting on the railway carriage with Miss Winifred, who invariably aroused his attention for a short while—he observed the pair, deciding he truly ought to address Grace regarding the matter and inform her that this behavior was improper. However, the minor event had slipped his mind by the moment he arrived at his residence. They swept past Mrs. Hector Twiss, who let out a scream of dismay, and they swept past Miss Clementine Ainslie, who chuckled and uttered a sigh. Ultimately, right before the swine darted into the rear yard of Bertie Shakespeare Drew, never to come out of it again because the trauma to their nervous systems was so severe—Grace and Edmund leaped down, at the exact moment Dr. and Mrs. Carrow sped past in their carriage.
{: #nw-v05-c12-p0010 }

“Thus you raise your young men,” stated Hugh with pretended seriousness.
{: #nw-v05-c12-p0011 }

“Maybe I indulge them slightly,” Nell remarked remorsefully, “however, oh, Hugh, whenever my mind returns to my early years prior to arriving at Grey Shutters, I lack the resolve to enforce rigid discipline. How desperate I felt for affection and amusement—a neglected young slavey who was denied any opportunity to enjoy herself! Their moments spent alongside the manse children are truly delightful.”
{: #nw-v05-c12-p0012 }

“What about the poor pigs?” Hugh asked.
{: #nw-v05-c12-p0013 }

Nell attempted to appear serious, but she was unsuccessful.
{: #nw-v05-c12-p0014 }

“Is it your genuine belief that it caused them pain?” she asked. “My impression is that nothing has the power to injure those creatures. Throughout this summer, they have acted as the local nuisance, yet the Drews refuse to confine them. Nevertheless, I shall speak with Edmund—provided I manage to suppress my laughter while doing so.”
{: #nw-v05-c12-p0015 }

That evening, Miss Winifred traveled to Hollowmere so she could vent her emotions regarding Sunday night. Upon arrival, she was amazed to discover that Nell failed to see Grace’s conduct from quite the same perspective as her own.
{: #nw-v05-c12-p0016 }

“It seemed to me that her going up in front of those churchgoers to make her confession held a certain courage and sadness,” she stated. “One could tell she was terrified out of her wits—and still, she was determined to vindicate her father. I adored her because of that.”
{: #nw-v05-c12-p0017 }

“Oh, naturally, the unfortunate girl had good intentions,” Miss Winifred sighed, “yet even so, it was an awful deed, which creates a greater stir than the Sabbath house-cleaning. That incident had started to fade, but this event has revived the whole matter. Clementine Ainslie shares your perspective—when departing from the church yesterday evening, she remarked that Grace’s action was brave, though it likewise filled her with pity for the girl. Miss Harriet viewed the entire affair as an amusing jest, stating that she had not enjoyed herself so much at church in years. Naturally, it matters little to them—being Episcopalians. However, we Presbyterians are affected by it. Furthermore, numerous hotel guests attended that evening, alongside dozens of Methodists. Mrs. Leander Crawford wept because of her deep distress. And Mrs. Hector Twiss declared that the young minx deserved a spanking.”
{: #nw-v05-c12-p0018 }

“In church, Mrs. Leander Crawford constantly weeps,” Tabitha remarked scornfully. “Any moving word from the minister brings her to tears. However, Mrs. Dr. dear, her signature rarely appears on a subscription list. Crying costs less. One time she attempted to converse with me regarding Aunt Martha’s filthy housekeeping; and I felt like replying, ‘Mrs. Leander Crawford, everybody is aware that you have been observed stirring up cakes inside the kitchen wash-pan!’ Nevertheless, Mrs. Dr. dear, I refrained from saying it, since my self-respect is too great for me to demean myself by disputing with someone like her. Yet, if I were inclined to spread rumors, I could reveal far worse matters concerning Mrs. Leander Crawford. Furthermore, regarding Mrs. Hector Twiss, had she uttered those words to me, Mrs. Dr. dear, do you realize what my response would have been? My reply would have been, ‘Mrs. Twiss, I do not question that spanking Grace would please you, but neither in this world nor in the one to come will you ever be afforded the opportunity to spank the daughter of a minister.’”
{: #nw-v05-c12-p0019 }

“Had poor Grace merely been dressed decently,” Miss Winifred lamented once more, “it would not have turned out entirely that terrible. However, standing on the platform there, she looked dreadful in that dress.”
{: #nw-v05-c12-p0020 }

“Mrs. Dr. dear, it was clean, nevertheless,” Tabitha stated. “Cleanliness is a trait of these children. Mrs. Dr. dear, they might possess a great deal of heedlessness and recklessness, a point I do not deny, yet washing behind their ears is something they never fail to do.”
{: #nw-v05-c12-p0021 }

“Imagine Grace failing to remember which day Sunday was,” Miss Winifred insisted. “Mark my words, she will become every bit as irresponsible and foolish as her father. I assume Rupert would have possessed more sense had he not been ill. The nature of his ailment escapes me, yet it seems highly probable that he had consumed the blueberries growing within the cemetery. It is no surprise they caused him to be unwell. Were I a Methodist, I would attempt to maintain the graveyard in a tidy state at the very least.”
{: #nw-v05-c12-p0022 }

“It is my belief that Rupert merely consumed the sours growing upon the dyke,” Tabitha remarked with optimism. “It seems unlikely to me that a minister’s child would consume blueberries which sprouted from the burial places of deceased folks. Eating items that developed on the dyke, Mrs. Dr. dear, wouldn't be quite so awful, as you know.”
{: #nw-v05-c12-p0023 }

“The initial part of yesterday evening’s display that was most awful was the expression Grace directed toward a person in the audience prior to commencing,” Miss Winifred stated. “Elder Clow asserts that she directed it toward him. Furthermore, was it brought to your attention that she was observed astride a pig during the day?”
{: #nw-v05-c12-p0024 }

“I spotted her. Edmund accompanied her. I offered him a slight—a quite slight—reprimand regarding the matter. He said little, yet he conveyed to me that the notion was his own and that Grace bore no fault.”
{: #nw-v05-c12-p0025 }

“I do not not believe that, Mrs. Dr. dear,” Tabitha exclaimed, fully defensive. “Edmund merely acts like that—assuming the fault personally. Yet you are just as aware as I am, Mrs. Dr. dear, that the sweet child would not ever conceive of sitting atop a pig, though he may compose poetry.”
{: #nw-v05-c12-p0026 }

“Oh, the idea was certainly born inside the mind of Grace Ashdown,” declared Miss Winifred. “And I cannot claim to regret that those elderly pigs belonging to Amos Drew finally received what they deserved for a change. However, it was the child of the minister!”
{: #nw-v05-c12-p0027 }

“And the doctor’s son!” Nell uttered, copying the manner of Miss Winifred. After that, she giggled. “Dear Miss Winifred, they are merely small children. Besides, you are aware that they have not performed a single evil act so far—they are simply thoughtless and rash—just as I used to be. They will become serious and grave—just as I have.”
{: #nw-v05-c12-p0028 }

Miss Winifred joined in the laughter, as well.
{: #nw-v05-c12-p0029 }

“At certain moments, Nell dearie, I can tell from your eyes that your serious manner is worn like a piece of clothing and you are actually desperate to act reckless and youthful once more. Well, my spirits are lifted. For some reason, a conversation with you constantly produces that result in me. Currently, whenever I pay a visit to Barbara Samson, the outcome is entirely reversed. I am made to feel by her that all things are amiss and shall forever remain so. Yet naturally, spending a whole lifetime with a husband such as Joe Samson would not prove to be particularly uplifting.”
{: #nw-v05-c12-p0030 }

“It is quite a peculiar thought that, despite all the opportunities she had, she ended up marrying Joe Samson,” Tabitha observed. “During her youth, she was greatly pursued. She would brag to me about having twenty-one suitors along with Mr. Pethick.”
{: #nw-v05-c12-p0031 }

“In what line was Mr. Pethick?”
{: #nw-v05-c12-p0032 }

“Indeed, he functioned as a kind of follower, Mrs. Dr. dear, though calling him a suitor would not be quite accurate. His intentions were not genuine, as a matter of fact. Twenty-one suitors—and myself having never possessed a single one! However, Barbara traversed the forest and selected the twisted branch in the end. Even so, it is claimed that her spouse is capable of preparing superior baking powder biscuits than she is, and she invariably asks him to prepare them whenever guests arrive for tea.”
{: #nw-v05-c12-p0033 }

“That brings to my mind that tomorrow guests are arriving at my place for tea, so I have to return home to make my bread dough,” Miss Winifred remarked. “Mary mentioned she was capable of making it, and I do not question that she could. Nevertheless, for as long as I am alive and active and existing, I mix my own bread dough, you can be sure of that.”
{: #nw-v05-c12-p0034 }

“How is Mary doing?” inquired Nell.
{: #nw-v05-c12-p0035 }

“I can’t complain about Mary,” Miss Winifred remarked somewhat sullenly. “Her frame is gaining weight, plus she is tidy and polite—even if she possesses more depth than I am able to comprehend. She is a cunning creature. Take my word for it, even a millennium of digging wouldn't allow you to reach the depths of that girl's thoughts! When it comes to labor, I have never witnessed anyone her equal. She devours it. Mrs. Grimble might have treated her with cruelty, yet people have no reason to claim she forced Mary to labor. Mary is a natural-born laborer. On occasion, I ponder whether her legs or her tongue will exhaust itself first. Lately, my own workload isn't sufficient to prevent me from causing trouble. The commencement of school will bring me genuine joy, because it means I will once more have tasks to occupy me. Mary has no desire to attend school, yet I took a firm stance and declared that her attendance was mandatory. I will refuse to let the Methodists claim I denied her an education while I relaxed lazily.”
{: #nw-v05-c12-p0036 }
